title: Apple to Launch Device Leasing Program With Klarna on July 28, Bloomberg Reports
excerpt: The program, called Apple Upgrade, will let U.S. customers lease iPhones and Macs through monthly payments, expanding the company’s push into consumer financing.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Apple's leasing program, Apple Upgrade, launches on July 28 in the U.S.
  • Klarna powers the program, enhancing its partnership with Apple since October 2024.
  • Customers can lease iPhones and Macs with monthly payments and upgrade options.
  • This marks Apple's significant shift towards hardware-as-a-service since 2024.
  • Leasing could lower costs and accelerate device upgrades for consumers.

  • Apple will launch a device leasing program called Apple Upgrade on July 28 in the United States, according to Bloomberg
  • The program is powered by Klarna, which has been an official Apple reseller since October 2024
  • Customers will be able to lease iPhones and Macs through monthly payments, with the option to upgrade at the end of the lease term
  • The move marks Apple’s most significant push into hardware-as-a-service since it scrapped an earlier subscription plan in 2024

Apple is launching a device leasing program called Apple Upgrade on July 28 in the United States to boost sales, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The program will be powered by Klarna, the Swedish buy-now-pay-later company that became an official Apple reseller in October 2024. Reuters confirmed the report, which sent Klarna shares higher in afternoon trading.

How Apple Upgrade Works

Under the existing Klarna partnership, customers can already purchase Apple Watch, iPad, and Mac products through monthly payment plans starting as low as $7.99 per month. At the end of the loan term, customers can trade in their device and upgrade to the latest model or keep their current device for a final interest-free payment.

The new Apple Upgrade program is expected to extend this model to a broader range of devices, including iPhones and Macs, according to multiple reports. APR rates range from 0% for qualified customers with excellent credit to 35.99% based on creditworthiness, with 24- or 36-month payment terms.

“It is super exciting that we’re simplifying the shopping experience for Apple products.”

— Sebastian Siemiatkowski, CEO of Klarna

Apple’s Financing Evolution

The launch represents Apple’s most aggressive move into hardware-as-a-service since Bloomberg reported in 2022 that the company was developing a monthly subscription model for iPhones; that project was scrapped in 2024 after software problems and regulatory concerns.

Apple currently offers the iPhone Upgrade Program through Citizens Bank, which splits iPhone purchases into installments over two years, with the option to upgrade after one year. It also offers Apple Card Monthly Installments for financing purchases.

In 2024, Apple discontinued its Apple Pay Later service and shifted to third-party financing through Affirm and Klarna via Apple Pay. The new Apple Upgrade program deepens that Klarna relationship significantly.

![Apple Watch. Why It Matters for Consumers

Apple’s premium pricing has long been a barrier for many consumers. The iPhone 16 Pro Max starts at $1,199, and the MacBook Pro at $1,999. A leasing model lowers the upfront cost and could accelerate upgrade cycles, which have stretched to over four years for many iPhone users.

For Apple, the program addresses a persistent challenge: roughly 60% of its installed base was still using older devices at last count. By making upgrades more financially accessible, the company aims to pull those holdouts into its latest ecosystem.

Market Impact

Klarna, which went public on the Nasdaq earlier this year, touts 25 million active users in the United States. The Apple partnership positions it as a central player in consumer electronics financing, competing with Affirm and traditional credit card installment plans.

Apple shares were trading near $235 in afternoon trading. The company reports third-quarter earnings on July 31, where executives are likely to face questions about the program’s potential impact on revenue recognition and device upgrade rates.

What to Watch

The July 28 launch will clarify which devices are included, pricing tiers, and whether the program will extend beyond the U.S. market. India, where Apple has been aggressively expanding its retail presence and consumer financing options, could be a natural next market for a similar leasing model.
nri_angle: The leasing program could make Apple’s premium devices more accessible to cost-conscious consumers in the U.S., including immigrants building credit histories.
